questions.q: Compound (X) [styrene] is subjected to the sequence of reactions: (i) Br2/CHCl3, (ii) NaNH2 (excess), (iii) CH3I, (iv) H2, Na/NH3 (l), giving the major product (Y). The molar mass of the major product (Y) formed is ____ g/mol. (Given molar mass in g/mol: C 12, H 1, O 16)
questions.explain: Go one step at a time. Br2 adds across the C=C of styrene to give Ph-CHBr-CH2Br. Excess NaNH2 removes two HBr (double elimination) and gives the terminal alkyne Ph-C≡CH, then pulls off its acidic H to give Ph-C≡C- Na+. CH3I is attacked by this anion (SN2) and gives Ph-C≡C-CH3, 1-phenylpropyne. Na/liquid NH3 reduces an alkyne to the trans alkene and leaves the benzene ring alone. So Y is trans-1-phenylpropene, Ph-CH=CH-CH3, formula C9H10. Molar mass = 9 x 12 + 10 x 1 = 118. The trap is 90 or 160, which come from stopping early or adding extra Br.

questions.q:
The compound (X) on
(i) heating in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 and HCl gas gives 2,4-dimethylpentane
(ii) aromatization gives toluene and
(iii) cyclisation gives methylcyclohexane.
The correct name of compound (X) is:
questions.explain: Use the product clues to find the carbon skeleton. AlCl3 with HCl isomerises a straight-chain alkane into a branched one. 2,4-Dimethylpentane has 7 carbons, so X is a 7-carbon straight chain. Aromatization of n-heptane over a Cr2O3 or V2O5 catalyst on alumina at high temperature gives toluene (C7H8). Cyclisation of n-heptane gives methylcyclohexane, which then loses hydrogen to give toluene. All three clues describe n-heptane, a saturated alkane. The alkene and triene options are traps: they have 7 carbons too, but isomerisation with AlCl3/HCl and these reactions are classic alkane behaviour.

questions.q:
Ph-CH=CH2 reacts with HBr in the presence of (PhCOO)2 to give a product. Consider the above reaction.
A. The reaction proceeds through a more stable radical intermediate.
B. The role of peroxide is to generate H• (hydrogen radical).
C. During this reaction, benzene is formed as a byproduct.
D. 1-Bromo-2-phenylethane is formed as the minor product.
E. The same reaction in absence of peroxide proceeds via carbocation intermediate.
Identify the correct statements. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explain: With peroxide, HBr adds against Markovnikov's rule by a radical path (the peroxide effect). The peroxide splits into PhCOO• radicals, which lose CO2 to give Ph•. Ph• takes H from HBr, giving benzene (a byproduct, so C is true) and a Br• radical. So the peroxide generates Br•, not H•, and B is false. Br• adds to the terminal CH2 to give the more stable benzylic radical, so A is true. The main product is 1-bromo-2-phenylethane, Ph-CH2-CH2-Br, so calling it the minor product (D) is false. Without peroxide the usual ionic path goes through a carbocation, so E is true. Correct: A, C and E.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements for the following reaction sequence: Compound X (molecular formula C3H6Cl2) + excess NaNH2 gives Compound Y. Y with dil. H2SO4/Hg2+ gives Compound Z. Y on heating in a red hot iron tube gives Compound Q (molecular formula C9H12).
Statement I: Compound Z will give a yellow precipitate with NaOI.
Statement II: Compound Q has two different types of H atoms (aromatic : aliphatic) in the ratio 1:3.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explain: X is a dichloropropane with both Cl on the same carbon or on neighbouring carbons (for example 2,2-dichloropropane or 1,2-dichloropropane). Excess NaNH2 removes 2 HCl and gives propyne, CH3-C≡CH (Y). Hydration of propyne with Hg2+/dil. H2SO4 follows Markovnikov's rule and gives acetone (Z) through the enol. Acetone has a CH3-CO- group, so it gives the yellow iodoform precipitate with NaOI. Statement I is true. Three propyne molecules trimerise in a red hot iron tube to give 1,3,5-trimethylbenzene (mesitylene), C9H12. It has 3 aromatic H and 9 methyl H, which is a ratio of 1:3. Statement II is true too.
